messages:
michelle (product): Quick announcement: we're formalizing a deprecation policy for the legacy SDK sync bindings (py/js) used in a lot of older internal samples. TL;DR — 12 month grace window, migration helpers, and automatic docs redirects. Please read the plan and give feedback by EOD Friday. :megaphone:

sam (eng): Thanks — can you paste the high-level dates? Need to know when to freeze CI checks for the old packages.

michelle (product): Timeline:
- Today: public RFC + docs update (this thread links it)
- 30 days: codemods + compat shim released (pip/npm packages)
- 6 months: start opt-in enforcement on CI (lint warnings -> failures optional per repo)
- 12 months: package sunset + docs removed from main landing; archives kept under /legacy/ with clear migration notes

kyle (docs): We'll add a migration guide and an explicit banner on the top of any page that references the old sync APIs. Draft banner text: `Deprecation notice: This SDK surface is deprecated. Migrate to the async/modern SDKs — see migration guide.` Thoughts?

maria (eng-infra): For Dedicated customers we should avoid any surprise breakage. Plan to add server-side fallback for the hosted API routing (keep supporting old client tokens for 12 months) and emit usage telemetry. Is telemetry opt-out?

michelle (product): Yes — telemetry will be aggregated and opt-outable per-org. We'll surface counts (calls, errors) to owners only. No payload content will be included.

ben (devex): I'm working on two migration helpers:
1) `redwood-compat` shim that maps old sync calls to the async runtime behind the scenes: `pip install redwood-compat`
2) an automated codemod for JS/TS to rewrite common patterns. We should publish examples in docs and in the samples repo.

sam (eng): Can we make the shim a feature-flagged package so infra teams can control rollout? Some customers embed the shim in build pipelines and we need a clean kill-switch.

ben (devex): Yep — feature flag + server-side kill switch. Default behavior will be a no-op passthrough unless org opts in. We'll document how to enable/disable.

kyle (docs): Action items for docs team:
- Draft migration guide + before/after code samples (deadline: 2 weeks)
- Add banner and redirect rules (by next week)
- Publish codemod walkthrough (with examples and rollback)
Assigning to @kyle and @james for edits.

michelle (product): Ops/eng: please add any compliance/regulatory flags that might affect Private customers. I'll coordinate with security and legal.

maria (eng-infra): We'll add CI lint rules as an opt-in first; schedule enforcement after 6 months. Will also add telemetry hooks to the console for owners to see migration progress.

sam (eng): One more ask — add a small compatibility matrix in the RFC showing which model runtimes and quantization formats are supported by the shim. That will help SRE and infra plan.

michelle (product): Good call. I'll update the RFC. Link to RFC + draft migration guide: https://redwood.example.internal/rfcs/2026-sdk-deprecation-plan (internal-only)

docs-bot: New doc pages created: `/docs/migration/legacy-sync-to-async` and `/docs/announcements/sdk-deprecation-2026`.

kyle (docs): I'll post a short Slack post in #general once the migration guide is live with a quick checklist for internal teams. :white_check_mark:

ben (devex): Plan for releasing codemod/shim in 30 days — beta channel first. Will add changelog and pinned issues for any repo owners who want early opt-in.

michelle (product): Thanks everyone. If you have any blocking concerns put them in this thread. We'll kick off a weekly sync starting next Tuesday to track progress.

sam (eng): Noted. I'll loop in release-manager for CI scheduling.

maria (eng-infra): Will create a dashboard to track old-sdk usage across orgs and send a weekly digest to owners.

kyle (docs): Copy. I'll prepare template PRs for the samples repo to demonstrate the migration flow.

michelle (product): End-of-thread checklist: RFC published, docs banner, codemod + shim planned, telemetry + opt-out, 12mo sunset. Thanks all. :pray:
